title: Unexpired Days on an Excess Flood Sale Cancellation When the Underlying Ends Early
content:
On an **Excess Flood Policies (Surplus Lines)** sale cancellation, the unexpired days are cut where the underlying primary policy ends before the excess term does.

**Rule.** The unexpired days stop short of the term end as follows: where the latest declarations on file for the underlying policy number on the policy record show the underlying policy expiring before the term end, the days from that expiration to the term end are removed; where the declarations show no earlier expiration but the underlying policy number on the policy record is that of a Tidemark HomeFlood policy whose own record shows its term ending before the excess term end, the days from that HomeFlood term end to the excess term end are removed; otherwise nothing is removed. Every number of days removed from the unexpired days is removed before the returned premium is figured.

The HomeFlood record read is that of the policy in HomeFlood Private Residential Flood Policies whose policy number is the underlying policy number on the excess policy record. Where two entries on a file share the date they are read by, or two policy records answer the same description, the one entered first is read.

| What the records show | Days removed |
|---|---|
| the latest declarations on file for the underlying policy number show an expiration before the excess term end | from that expiration to the excess term end |
| no such earlier expiration on the declarations; the underlying policy number is a Tidemark HomeFlood policy whose term ends before the excess term end | from the HomeFlood term end to the excess term end |
| neither | none |

**Worked illustration (hypothetical).** A 365-day excess term ending on 31 December, sale cancellation with 200 unexpired days before any cut; the latest declarations show the underlying expiring on 1 December, 30 days before the excess term end. The unexpired days become 170.
